UI_MinidoracatAutoDrive_HUDOptionsDescri: Shown above the vanilla vehicle dashboard. Theme and layout changes apply immediately.
UI_MinidoracatAutoDrive_OptionsDescripti: Autodrive trajectory, driver HUD, and optional diagnostic-log settings. Line width changes client pixel fill only and adds no server load. Diagnostic logs are off by default. Trajectory and HUD changes apply immediately.
UI_MinidoracatAutoDrive_ShowTrajectory_t: Shows the future driving line only while autodrive is engaged. Blue is the normal path and yellow is an obstacle-avoidance path. Disabling it does not affect autodrive.
UI_MinidoracatAutoDrive_TrajectoryWidth_: Adjusts the single autodrive trajectory line. Thin, standard, and thick use 1, 3, and 7 pixels. Each segment is still drawn once; this adds only a small amount of client pixel fill and does not affect the server.
UI_MinidoracatAutoDrive_HUDPolicyToggle: Player choice: click to toggle; this affects your vehicle only.
UI_MinidoracatAutoDrive_HUDPolicyLocked: Locked by the server sandbox policy.
UI_MinidoracatAutoDrive_HUDPolicyLockedO: The server policy forces this slowdown on; players cannot disable it.
The server policy forces this slowdown off. Only this dedicated speed cap is removed; all other safety limits remain active.
UI_MinidoracatAutoDrive_HUDZombieTipOn:
Detection: individual zombies %1–%2 metres ahead and within %3 metres to either side of the driving line.
Enabled: 1–3 zombies cap speed at %4, 4–7 at %5, and 8 or more at %6 km/h.
Zombies are not obstacles: AutoDrive does not swerve or stop for them; it slows down and drives through them.
UI_MinidoracatAutoDrive_HUDZombieTipOff:
Detection: individual zombies %1–%2 metres ahead and within %3 metres to either side of the driving line.
Disabled: zombie count adds no dedicated speed cap.
Zombies remain non-obstacles. Obstacle avoidance, blocked-road braking, following, cornering, and other safety limits still apply.
UI_MinidoracatAutoDrive_HUDCorpseTipOn:
Detection: corpses on the ground %1–%2 metres ahead and within %3 metres to either side of the driving line.
Enabled: one or more corpses cap speed at %4 km/h; additional corpses do not create further tiers.
Corpses are not obstacles: AutoDrive does not swerve or stop for them; it slows down and drives over them.
UI_MinidoracatAutoDrive_HUDCorpseTipOff:
Detection: corpses on the ground %1–%2 metres ahead and within %3 metres to either side of the driving line.
Disabled: corpses add no dedicated speed cap.
Corpses remain non-obstacles. Obstacle avoidance, blocked-road braking, following, cornering, and other safety limits still apply.
UI_MinidoracatAutoDrive_ExportTelemetry_: Off by default. When enabled, this client writes autodrive diagnostic logs containing absolute world coordinates (x/y) and raw Unix epoch milliseconds with no timezone conversion. Logs stay on this computer: 64 slots, up to 2 MiB each. The setting takes effect on the next AutoDrive session. Starting a new log clears expired slots for reuse but keeps their filenames. A full slot stops appending for that drive and never overwrites its beginning. Do not share a log unless you intend to reveal both coordinates and activity times.
UI_MinidoracatAutoDrive_TelemetryRetenti: How long to keep diagnostic logs on this computer: 1, 3, 7, 14, or 30 days (default 7). Starting a new log clears expired slots for reuse but keeps their filenames. Does not affect driving.
UI_MinidoracatAutoDrive_CopyLatestTeleme: Copies the absolute path of the latest diagnostic log file to the clipboard so you can send one file when reporting a problem. Success normally uses a top-right toast; an older framework or Toast failure falls back to an overhead notice. The log contains absolute world coordinates (x/y) and raw Unix epoch milliseconds.
UI_MinidoracatAutoDrive_CopyTelemetryFol: Copies the absolute path of the local diagnostic-log folder. It contains 64 fixed log slots plus three small management files: manifest.txt, latest.txt, and session-index.txt. session-index.txt maps raw Unix epoch milliseconds to each session log with no timezone conversion. Logs contain absolute world coordinates (x/y); do not share the whole folder.
UI_MinidoracatAutoDrive_TelemetryCopied: Diagnostic log path copied to the clipboard
UI_MinidoracatAutoDrive_TelemetryCopyFai: Could not copy the diagnostic log path
UI_MinidoracatAutoDrive_TelemetrySlotsFu: None of the 64 diagnostic log slots could be cleared for reuse; this drive will not be recorded
UI_MinidoracatAutoDrive_TelemetryWriteFa: Diagnostic logging failed; recording has stopped for this drive
UI_MinidoracatAutoDrive_TelemetryFileFul: The diagnostic log reached its 2 MiB limit; this drive will not append more data
